title: Impact of Recent Fires in Australia on Singapore’s Environment and Food Security
what_it_is: Impact of Recent Fires in Australia on Singapore’s Environment and Food Security

sections.label: Australian fires and Singapore food security
sections.summary: Singapore's air quality stayed Good or Moderate and food supply from Australia remained steady during the November 2019 to January 2020 fires.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: From November 2019 to January 2020, when the fires took place, air quality in Singapore was mostly in the "Good" and "Moderate" range.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Similarly, Singapore’s food security has not been affected by the fires in Australia.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: While many parts of Australia experienced the fires, our food supply from Australia remained steady between November 2019 and January 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we are mindful that disruptions in food imports, including those linked to the climate, remain a possibility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Hence, the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) has been working with food importers to diversify sources across different countries and to adopt plans to mitigate against supply disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Apart from this, we are encouraging Singapore companies to build food production linkages with other countries under our "Grow Overseas" strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are also intensifying efforts to boost domestic food production under our "30 by 30" vision, to locally produce 30% of Singapore’s nutritional needs by 2030.

sections.label: 30 by 30 vision progress
sections.summary: The question asks how on track the 30 by 30 vision is and whether it needs to be accelerated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: My question is: given what is happening around the world, how are we on track to achieve it, and is there a need for this "30 by 30" vision to be, in fact, accelerated?

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We have never had a situation where the fires in Australia would actually affect Singapore.

sections.label: Food security and 30 by 30
sections.summary: Food security will be a main Committee of Supply topic, and Singapore must grow food itself despite water, land and energy constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: On food security: indeed, this is going to be one of the main topics in our Ministry's Committee of Supply, to get Singaporeans to understand that beyond diversifying our food supplies, we really have to be serious about looking at growing the food ourselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Because in Singapore, we are very constrained by water, land, even by energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: So, these are the constraints that Singapore has to overcome but I am very confident that with technology and perseverance, we will get to the target of "30 by 30" that we set ourselves to achieve.
